rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for anticipating that an event will happen.

example.english: I expect it will rain tomorrow.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jyu6 gai3 ting1 jat6 wui5 lok6 jyu5

rows.note: Use this when “expect” means imposing a duty or requirement rather than predicting an event.

example.english: I expect you to hand in the report today.
example.traditional: 我要求你今日交份報告。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jiu1 kau4 nei5 gam1 jat6 gaau1 fan6 bou3 gou3

rows.note: Use this for expecting someone to achieve something or for expectations placed on them, without necessarily stating a requirement.

example.english: I expect you to get good marks in this exam.
example.traditional: 我期望你今次考試攞到好成績。
example.jyutping: ngo5 kei4 mong6 nei5 gam1 ci3 haau2 si5 lo2 dou3 hou2 sing4 zik1

rows.note: Use this specifically for being pregnant or expecting a baby, not for predicting an event.

example.english: I hear they expect a baby.
example.jyutping: teng1 gong2 keoi5 dei6 jau5 zo2 bi1 bi1
